$comment: Both Minnesota city rates run at $16.37 -- roughly $5 above the state's own $11.41, the largest local-over-state gap of any state in this database. Saint Paul's smaller tiers step on JULY 1, so a January-only refresh understates them for half the year.

jurisdictions.name: Minneapolis
jurisdictions.coverage: ALL employers regardless of size, and all employees regardless of age. Minneapolis's own large/small employer split ended when the small-business schedule caught up.

tipped.note: Minnesota bars any tip credit statewide, so the full local rate is owed in cash.

sources.title: City of Minneapolis -- Minimum wage increases to $16.37 for all employers
sources.verifiedBy: cross_source_confirmed this session: $16.37 for all employers effective 2026-01-01.

sources.title: City of Minneapolis -- Minimum Wage (2027)
sources.verifiedBy: City of Minneapolis Minimum Wage https://minimumwage.minneapolismn.gov/ read directly 2026-11-06: 'In 2026, the Minneapolis Minimum Wage is $16.37. On January 1, 2027, it will increase to $17.02.' Tips do not count toward the wage.

variants.label: Small businesses (6-100 employees), from July 1, 2027
variants.test: Small catches up to the large rate on 2027-07-01.

variants.label: Micro businesses (5 or fewer employees), January 1 - June 30, 2027
Micro businesses (5 or fewer employees), from July 1, 2027
Youth aged 14-17, first 90 days
variants.test: After 90 days a youth employee moves to the rate for the employer's size tier. The 2027 youth rate was not in the city's announcement; the city's rule is 85% of the small-business rate rounded up to the nickel, which would be $13.95 while small is $16.37 and $14.50 once small is $17.02 on 2027-07-01 (not applied).

tipped.note: No tip credit -- Minnesota state law.

sources.title: City of Saint Paul -- Minimum Wage Increases for Small and Micro Businesses (effective July 1, 2026)
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched and read directly this session. Quoted: 'The minimum wage hourly rate will be: $16.37 for small businesses (6-100 employees) $14.25 for micro businesses (5 employees or fewer)', plus the $13.95 youth rate for ages 14-17 during the first 90 days. CORRECTED to record BOTH halves of 2026 (small $15.00/micro $13.25 Jan-Jun, $16.37/$14.25 Jul-Dec) -- matching the same before/after-mid-year-step pattern already used for Renton's and Everett's WA ordinances elsewhere in this database, rather than only the half in effect on this file's own asOf date.

sources.title: City of Saint Paul -- 2027 minimum wage rates
sources.verifiedBy: City of Saint Paul, Announcing City of Saint Paul Minimum Wage Rates for 2027 (September 1, 2026) https://www.stpaul.gov/news/announcing-city-saint-paul-minimum-wage-rates-2027 read directly 2026-11-06: effective January 1, 2027 $17.02 for large and macro businesses (101+ employees), $16.37 for small (6-100), $14.25 for micro (5 or fewer); effective July 1, 2027 $17.02 large, $17.02 small, $15.00 micro.

sources.title: UC Berkeley Labor Center -- Inventory of US City and County Minimum Wage Ordinances
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched and read directly this session. The standing national census of local minimum wage ordinances -- used here to establish WHICH jurisdictions exist (so none is silently omitted), with each rate then cross-checked against a second source.

knownGaps: Saint Paul's macro (10,001+) and large (101-10,000) tiers are both at $16.37 in 2026 and are recorded as one entry; they diverge in earlier years.

provisional.note: Carried forward from the 2026 file on 2026-10-25 so that a 2027-dated query resolves instead of failing. Every figure is 2026's unless listed in updatedFor2027 (each with the state agency's own announcement or the statute). Remove this block only after every figure has been re-read against a 2027 source. LOCAL ORDINANCES ARE NOT YET UPDATED for 2027: many step on 1 January 2027 (e.g. Denver $19.84, Minneapolis $17.02, Seattle, Flagstaff, Albuquerque, Portland ME). The figures here are 2026's until each ordinance is re-read.
